summary: The root مري (mry) primarily means to stroke or rub, especially to draw forth milk from a she-camel.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.

headwords.def: الرِّيحُ تَمْرِى السَّحَابَ and The wind draws forth the clouds. (M, TA.) See an ex. in a verse cited voce عَزْلَآءُ.

inf. n. مُمَارَاةٌ and مِرَآءٌ, i. q. جَادَلَهُ; (S, K; *) He disputed with him, or did so obstinately, &c.: (TA:) it is only in opposing [what has been said; not in commencing a disputation]. (Msb.)
The disputing, or contending, together. (TA.) You say, هُمَا يَتَمَارَيَانِ بِالشِّعْرِ [ They two dispute, or contend, together, with verses or poetry ]. (TA in art. بده.)
He doubted, به of it. (Kur, xliii. 61.) See 1.
اِسْتَمْرَتِ الإِبِلُ المحَمْضَ for اِسْتَمْرَأَتْهُ: see 1 in art. عدن.
A certain plant: see خَافُورٌ, and حَبَقٌ, and فَاخُورٌ.

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
